author: storage-namespace repair lane
binds: This artifact binds NOTHING. It is a candidate successor to artifacts/threat-model.v3.json#/storageNamespace offered for independent review. It is not applied, not registered, not pinned, and carries no verdict, seal, disposition or status of its own beyond the four declarations above. Under IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §7.2 a version number binds nothing and only a digest does; under §7.2.1 an artifact is frozen at dispatch, so these bytes are final for whatever review is dispatched against them and any continuation belongs in a successor to THIS file.

predecessor.recordingObligation: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §7.2 requires a successor to record the filename and SHA-256 of every input its content depends on, as data, not as a count and not as prose. verifiedInputs below is that record.
predecessor.editDiscipline: §7.2 forbids editing reviewed bytes in place. artifacts/threat-model.v3.json is not modified by this work; this file is a successor and a derivation, never an edit. The predecessor's digest is unchanged and was re-measured after this file was written.

subtreeDigestsReproduced.note: The independent review recorded three serialisations of $.storageNamespace. All three were re-derived here and hard-compared, per §7.2.2's rule that a recorded measurement must be compared to the measurement it records.

whereThisGoesFurtherThanTheProposedRepai: SN-IR-01: the reviewer proposed 'resolution MUST obtain the root locator from the authority record and MUST refuse unless rootId is byte-equal'. That is a comparison, and a comparison has to be sited. SN-P1 instead removes the argument position, so a disagreeing root is not refused — it cannot be expressed. The byte-equality test remains, but it now guards a value that has exactly one producer instead of guarding one of two competing inputs.

SN-IR-02: the reviewer's conflict criterion was 'equal rootId, different canonical path'. That re-promotes the path to a decision procedure one clause after demoting it. SN-P2 states uniqueness as a FUNCTION property of the authority-record set and uses the locator only as a presence probe, so the criterion is 'two live locators', which is the identity owner's own criterion and does not depend on the path being authoritative.

SN-IR-03: the reviewer named EXDEV. Measured on a real nested mount, the mount-point case can also present as EBUSY, so naming an errno would have under-specified the property; SN-P3 is stated as a device-identity and mount-point property with the errnos as examples. The reviewer also asked what the recovery table's closure property becomes if a row is added — the answer developed here is that NO row is admissible, because a refusal that persists no transition contributes no point to a domain whose members are durable states, and the resulting observed tuple is already row 1.

theFinding.oneSentence: The physical namespace is the pair (admitted root, ProjectId); the ProjectId half is total, injective and collision-free, and the root half was bound by no rule.
theFinding.theCommonCause: PROJECT-ID-V1 gives its identity TWO custody records — the project marker and the host registry — with a uniqueness constraint between them, and forbids callers from supplying it. rootId had ONE custody record, the root marker, no uniqueness constraint, and no rule about who may supply a root. All three blockers are consequences of that single asymmetry, which is why this candidate repairs the asymmetry rather than the three symptoms.

howEachBlockerFollows.SN-IR-01: With no rule forbidding a supplied root, the root stayed an independent input, so nothing ever had to read activeRootId — hence a durable field with zero specified consumers.
howEachBlockerFollows.SN-IR-02: With no registry-side uniqueness constraint, rootId uniqueness could only ever be a create-time procedure, so copying reproduced it.
howEachBlockerFollows.SN-IR-03: With the root unbound, 'admitted root' was only ever a path-containment scope, so the rename precondition was expressed as containment and the device property was never stated.

blockerDisposition.reviewerTitle: The authority record is specified only as a migration artifact; ordinary storage resolution has no stated root-identity validation, and the record has no specified creation.
blockerDisposition.propertyUsed: SN-P1 (resolution is unary) with SN-P4 (creation is compare-and-swap at generation 0 -> 1).
blockerDisposition.failingScenarioThePredecessorAdmits: A verified ProjectId P has durable evidence under root R_auth, whose authority record reads activeRootId = rootId(R_auth). A user or policy selects a different, entirely well-formed admitted root R_decoy. The predecessor's admittedStorageRoot.admission validates R_decoy's storage-root.v1.json for shape, succeeds, and layout.projectNamespace then yields R_decoy/projects/P, which is created fresh. P now has two physical namespaces and the predecessor states no corruption signal for it.
blockerDisposition.measured: Executed. Both rule sets were implemented from prose and run against a real filesystem. The predecessor decider returned RESOLVED at the decoy root, created the second namespace while the first still held its ledger bytes, and the read-set of the authority record it consulted was the EMPTY SET — no field of the record was read, which is the same fact the review measured statically as 'zero specified consumers'.
blockerDisposition.mechanismThatNowRejectsIt: There is no argument position for R_decoy. Resolution takes only P; it reads activeRootId and the advisory locator from P's record, opens what the locator names, and proceeds only on byte-equality of that root's rootId with activeRootId. Offering a root to a resolution path is STORAGE_ROOT_CALLER_SUPPLIED. Measured: the successor decider returned STORAGE_ROOT_CALLER_SUPPLIED when the root was offered, RESOLVED at R_auth when it was not, and its read-set of the record was exactly {activeRootId, activeRootCanonicalPath}.
blockerDisposition.andWhenTheHintItselfLies: With activeRootCanonicalPath repointed at R_decoy, the successor returned STORAGE_ROOT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH rather than resolving. That is the test that separates a dispositive identity from an authoritative path: the advisory field was wrong and the answer was still not wrong.
blockerDisposition.creation: SN-P4 gives the record the birth it lacked, and gives it no new mechanism: create-new plus fsync at generation 1 under the authority lease IS the compare-and-swap with an empty baseline.

blockerDisposition.reviewerTitle: rootId uniqueness is asserted only at allocation. Duplication of a storage root by copy is unhandled.
blockerDisposition.propertyUsed: SN-P2 (root-instance uniqueness as an invariant of the authority-record set, evaluated at open time).
blockerDisposition.failingScenarioThePredecessorAdmits: An admitted root at /store carrying rootId X is copied whole to /store-backup by an ordinary recursive copy. The copy's storage-root.v1.json is byte-identical, so its rootId is X. Both roots are present. The copy is offered for admission.
blockerDisposition.measured: Executed with a real recursive copy. The copy reproduced rootId byte-for-byte and the two roots were distinct canonical paths. The predecessor decider returned RESOLVED on the copy. The successor decider returned STORAGE_ROOT_COLLISION.
blockerDisposition.mechanismThatNowRejectsIt: The live authority-record set binds X to the locator /store. Admission of a root bearing X at a different canonical locator probes the bound locator, finds it PRESENT and bearing X, and refuses with STORAGE_ROOT_COLLISION. Neither root is selected and no namespace beneath either is opened. The invariant is a property of the record set — the relation activeRootId -> activeRootCanonicalPath is a function — so it is evaluated every time that set is read, not once at allocation, which is what makes it reach a copy made outside the tool.
blockerDisposition.andTheGenuineMoveIsNotCaughtWithIt: The same scenario with a rename instead of a copy — so the bound locator is ABSENT — returned STORAGE_ROOT_LOCATOR_STALE, the precondition for the one permitted atomic rebind under explicit adopt. Measured. A rule that refused both would be safe and useless; the discriminator is liveness of the bound locator, exactly as it is for PROJECT-ID-V1's rootMove.
blockerDisposition.whyNotACreateTimeCheck: Copying happens outside the tool. A create-time check cannot observe it at all, which is why the review is right that the repair had to be an invariant and not a procedure.

blockerDisposition.reviewerTitle: The purge commit path depends on an intra-root atomic rename, but the artifact never requires an admitted root to be a single filesystem.
blockerDisposition.propertyUsed: SN-P3 (one device across the layout-derived rename operand set), stated once at pathSafety.resolution and typed into pathSafety.unsupported's existing predicate domain.
blockerDisposition.failingScenarioThePredecessorAdmits: A filesystem is mounted at projects/<ProjectId> beneath an otherwise valid admitted root — a dedicated volume, an external disk or a network mount for one project's data. The predecessor admits the root: path containment holds, and pathSafety.unsupported enumerates capabilities of a filesystem, in which 'the root is one filesystem' is not expressible. Purge then runs: the moving marker is written and fsynced inside the canonical namespace, and the atomic rename of the namespace into quarantine is attempted.
blockerDisposition.measured: Executed against a REAL nested mount created for this purpose on the authoring host, not simulated. The moving marker was written. The rename returned errno 18, EXDEV, Cross-device link. Durable state afterwards: journal PREPARED, canonical present, quarantine absent. Root admission under the predecessor's rules succeeded; under SN-P3 it returned STORAGE_ROOT_NOT_ONE_DEVICE.
blockerDisposition.mechanismThatNowRejectsIt: The root never reaches purge. SN-P3 is established at admission from the retained root handle, before any user-derived durable write, and a root whose layout-derived rename operand scope does not resolve to one device identity is refused with a typed outcome. The predicate ranges over directories, whose set the layout bounds; the measurement above also shows why it must range one level below projects/ rather than over the three top-level host-managed directories, since the device split was at projects/<ProjectId> while projects/, control/ and quarantine/ all agreed.
blockerDisposition.whyNoSeventhRow: The refused rename persists no transition, so the durable state after it is identical to the state before it: PREPARED, canonical present, quarantine absent. That tuple IS row 1 of the closed 6-row table. The table's domain is durable state, so an operation that persists nothing contributes no point to it and requires no row. The closure property and the test for when a further row WOULD be admissible are stated at rootBinding.renameAtomicity.recoveryTableClosure, so a seventh row cannot be added silently.
blockerDisposition.whatTheReviewerNamedAndWhatWasMeasuredIn: The review named EXDEV. A mount point can also make the rename fail as EBUSY rather than EXDEV depending on platform and on whether the mount is at or beneath the renamed directory, so SN-P3 is stated as a device-identity and mount-point property and treats the errnos as examples. Binding the property to one errno spelling would have been the §6 law 18 mistake in a different register.

nonInterferenceWithTheSection46PurgeDisc.question: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §4.6 records V10 item 3 — purge semantics — as DISCHARGED on retention-tiers.v23 Part B, independently reviewed PASS at 0 blockers. Does the SN-IR-03 repair disturb that discharge?
nonInterferenceWithTheSection46PurgeDisc.answer: No, and the reason is structural rather than incidental.
why: §4.6's discharge is about what purge MEANS for evidence availability given that a purge occurs: the effective_capability derivation, the four v22 fixtures including AF-03-VERIFY-PURGED, seal-blindness in the strong form result == min(sealed, best), and the 40,000-trial result that purge never raises capability. SN-P3 changes WHICH ROOTS MAY HOLD EVIDENCE AT ALL. It never changes what a purge means when one runs.

The repair adds no purge state, no reason code, no deficiency member, no error code, no availability outcome and no transition. It does not touch purge.states, purge.reachableDurableNonterminalStates, purge.operationOrdering, purge.crashRecoveryTable, purge.crashFixtures or purge.recoveryRule — no operation in this derivation addresses any of those paths.
The deletion commit point is unmoved: VERIFIED_ABSENT is still reached by the same step in the same order.

A root refused by SN-P3 is refused before any user-derived durable write, so it holds no evidence, hosts no sealed Run and can be the subject of no purge. The set of purges over which §4.6 quantifies is unchanged; the set of roots that can host one is narrowed, and narrowing it strictly toward roots on which the commit can actually be performed.
Measured non-overlap: retention-tiers.v24.json contains 0 occurrences of 'storageNamespace' and check-retention-custody-v24.py contains 0. The surfaces do not read each other.
nonInterferenceWithTheSection46PurgeDisc.ifThisIsWrongItIsWrongLoudly: Stated plainly as required: if a reviewer judges that refusing a multi-device root narrows the domain §4.6's discharge quantifies over in a way that matters, that is a conflict with a DISCHARGED item and must be escalated under IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §8, not absorbed. This candidate's position is that it does not, for the reasons above, and the position is falsifiable: exhibit a purge whose availability semantics differ because its root spans two devices.

Resolution has no selection step at all. The implementer no longer has to decide whether a selected root or a named root wins, because only one of them is an input.
Byte-equality of the opened root's storage-root.v1.json rootId against the record's activeRootId, performed after landing and before any namespace is opened, with a named outcome on failure.

create-new plus fsync at generation 1 under the authority lease at first durable write, ordered after root admission and before namespace creation, with the crash cases in both gaps stated. It is the existing compare-and-swap with an empty baseline, so nothing new is introduced to build.

A device-identity and mount-point property over the layout-derived directory scope, established at admission from the retained root handle, with a named outcome, a stated scan reach, and a stated runtime residual.

knownLimitations: CROSS-MACHINE. SN-P2 is a machine-local invariant over the local authority-record set. A root copied to a machine with no record binding its rootId is admitted there, exactly as PROJECT-ID-V1's crossMachineHonesty admits a marker carried to a machine with no registry history. The refusal to claim more is inherited deliberately: the host cannot prove a remote conflicting root without network authority and this candidate does not claim to. If both copies are later opened on one machine, the second admission trips STORAGE_ROOT_COLLISION.

RESTORE OVER THE ORIGINAL LOCATION. A backup restored on top of the original path presents one rootId at one locator and is indistinguishable from the original by any rule stated here or in the identity owner. This candidate does not detect it and does not claim to. Whether restored content can resurrect purged bytes is a retention and deletion question owned elsewhere, and no verdict is offered on it.

THE ADMISSION SCAN'S REACH. SN-P3's admission scan observes directories. A file-level bind mount, and any mount created after admission, are outside it. Neither is absorbed silently — the rename refuses and persists nothing, and the next admission refuses the root — but the property is established at admission over a stated scope rather than continuously, and this is a bound, not a totality claim.

PATH LENGTH remains untreated, as the review's NB-01 records. Nothing here changes it, and SN-P3's admission-time root properties are the natural place for it if a coordinator wants NB-01 closed. It was left alone as out of scope for these three blockers, and it is the observation nearest to becoming a fourth.
THE NEW MATERIAL IS UNENFORCED. rootBinding has no retained checker. See checkerImpact.paperSealDisclosure.
NO RUNTIME CLAIM. Every property here is a property of text. Whether a built host honours any of them is release-gated under G14 and unobservable in this corpus.

anticipatedObjections.objection: SN-P1 says a root cannot be supplied, but a specification cannot delete an argument position in someone else's implementation — so this is still just a rule, and rules get missed.
anticipatedObjections.response: Correct, and it is the strongest objection to this candidate. The claim is precisely scoped: at the SPECIFICATION level the bad state becomes inexpressible, because the contract defines resolution as unary and no conforming API can accept a root. At the IMPLEMENTATION level conformance is a runtime property no instrument here can observe, and rootBinding.observabilityBoundary says exactly that rather than pretending otherwise. What changed is that an implementer following this specification cannot arrive at the defect by omission — which is the specific failure E-NS-1 records — not that a non-conforming host is prevented.

anticipatedObjections.objection: Seven new outcome identifiers is an enumeration, which is the thing the repair was supposed to avoid.
anticipatedObjections.response: The enumeration is of OUTCOMES, not of sites. Each value is produced by exactly one property and consumed by the identity owner's existing provenance rule; the set is closed and its members are named so that a refusal cannot be silent. The identity owner carries seven of its own for the same reason. What would have been the forbidden shape is a rule added at each place the root is used, and there is none.

anticipatedObjections.objection: The declared provenance mapping touches D9.
anticipatedObjections.response: It does not. No D9 class, error code, exit code or axis value is minted, and identityOutcomeD9Mapping is not modified — no operation addresses resolved-inputs.v2.json at all, which this candidate cannot edit in any case. What is declared is which of the identity owner's three EXISTING provenance values each new outcome carries, which is the rule that artifact already binds for exactly this purpose. A reviewer who judges that even this is out of scope can strike outcomes.definitions[*].provenance without disturbing any property.

anticipatedObjections.objection: rootBinding is unenforced, so this is a paper repair.
anticipatedObjections.response: Partly true and disclosed rather than argued away. The alternative was to add fixtures to storageNamespace.fixtures, whose closed set equality the pinned checker enforces, which would have broken check-threat-claims.py on application and forced a checker into the same act — and this lane may not write one. The choice was between an honest unenforced sibling and a repair that cannot be applied. checkerImpact names exactly what a successor checker must bind, in enough detail to be built from.

anticipatedObjections.objection: SN-P3's scan is O(directories) and admission now walks the tree.
anticipatedObjections.response: Stated in the artifact at properties.SN-P3.admissionCost. The scan does not range over CAS objects, which is where the size is. A reviewer may still judge the cost unacceptable for a root holding many projects, in which case the property is unchanged and only the point at which it is established would move — which would reopen exactly the mid-state-machine discovery this repair exists to prevent, and should be resisted.

anticipatedObjections.objection: The claim that no seventh recovery row is needed depends on the refused rename persisting nothing, which is a claim about an implementation.
anticipatedObjections.response: It is a claim about the ORDER the predecessor already specifies: the journal is persisted PREPARED before the namespace changes, and QUARANTINED only after the rename and the parent fsyncs. A rename that does not occur therefore sits between two persisted states and changes neither. It was also measured on a real filesystem. The falsification condition is stated: exhibit a step that can persist a state outside the closed set.

residualsRaisedNotRepaired.statement: rootBinding is not mechanically enforced. checkerImpact lists the six assertions a successor checker must carry.

The review's NB-01 (path length untreated corpus-wide, quarantine layouts roughly double path depth during the recovery-critical operations, Windows MAX_PATH exposure) is untouched here and remains open.

The review's NB-03 (check-threat-claims.py asserts declared fixture violations are a SUBSET of computed violations rather than equal to them, at line 526) is a checker defect this lane may not repair.

The review's NB-04 (SN-01..SN-04 are cited by five fixtures but defined only inside the checker) is untouched. The new vectors avoid reproducing it by naming properties that are defined in the artifact itself.

The review left open whether a non-COMPLETE purge journal on a source root can coexist with an in-flight migration of the same ProjectId, and whether an incomplete purge on a root later migrated away from becomes undiscoverable. correspondence.note: 'A raw caller/config ProjectId never becomes authority' becomes 'a raw caller/config ROOT never becomes authority', one level up.

The owner already writes 'They may select a root; only the host reads or allocates its marker.' The predecessor's unreconciled selection/naming pair is that same distinction, left unstated for the storage root.
The owner's unique constraint lives in the registry, not in the marker. The predecessor gave the root only the marker half, which is exactly why copying duplicated it.
Reserve, then publish create-new plus fsync, then commit; crash recovery completes an exact match and refuses anything else.
'ordinary analysis never silently adopts' is inherited in force.
Same criterion — one identity resolving while that identity is bound to another LIVE locator — and the same consequence: neither is selected implicitly.
Absence of the bound locator plus one newly opened canonical locator permits one atomic rebind; two live roots or non-identical marker bytes are refused.
Explicit adopt after proving absence, or explicit fork that re-allocates.
The owner declines to claim what it cannot prove without network authority. The root half inherits that refusal rather than pretending to a stronger property.

identityOwnerAgreement.whatIsNotInherited: The owner's outcome names, its D9 context table, its golden vectors and its eight-candidate allocation retry are its own. This section names them, uses their shapes, and copies none of them.

SN-P1.title: Storage resolution is unary: the root is a derived value, never an input.
SN-P1.statement: Storage resolution is a total function of exactly one input, the host-verified typed ProjectId. The root locator it uses is obtained only by reading that ProjectId's single authority record, and the only root it accepts is one whose storage-root.v1.json rootId is byte-equal to that record's activeRootId. No caller, configuration key, profile, policy, environment value or command flag has an argument position by which a root may be supplied to a resolution path; a root presented on one is STORAGE_ROOT_CALLER_SUPPLIED.
SN-P1.whyThisIsStructuralAndNotASiteList: It adds no comparison at the sites where the defect appears. It removes the argument position, so the bad state has nowhere to be written down. The predecessor's defect was never a missing check — it was an extra input, and a rule that deletes an input cannot be evaded by finding a site the rule forgot.
SN-P1.consumerConsequence: activeRootId acquires a consumer by construction rather than by enumeration: it is the sole producer of the root half of every canonical path the layout defines. A durable field with no reader cannot enforce an isolation boundary; a field that is the only producer of a value cannot fail to be read without the value failing to exist.
SN-P1.dispositiveVersusAdvisory: activeRootId is dispositive — it decides. activeRootCanonicalPath is an advisory locator that says only where to look. Landing somewhere is never a decision; the decision is the byte-equality test performed after landing.
SN-P1.theAdvisoryLocatorIsAnExactAccelerator: IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 law 8 already governs this shape: an exact accelerator is rebuildable and 'neither cache absence nor cache corruption may become a false empty or clean result'. A stale locator therefore yields STORAGE_ROOT_LOCATOR_STALE and an explicit adopt — never a fresh namespace, never a different root. The demotion of the path is derived from a law this freeze already carries rather than invented here.
SN-P1.whatThisAlsoCloses: A moved storage root becomes re-bindable BY IDENTITY instead of unresolvable, because the thing that decides is the one thing a move does not change.

SN-P2.title: Root-instance uniqueness is an invariant of the authority-record set, evaluated at open time.
SN-P2.statement: Across the live authority-record set, the relation activeRootId -> activeRootCanonicalPath is a FUNCTION: no two live records may name one activeRootId at two different canonical locators. This is an invariant of the record set, evaluated whenever that set is read under the authority lease. It is not a step in an allocation procedure and does not depend on when any rootId was minted.
SN-P2.openTimeDetection: Admitting a root whose storage-root.v1.json rootId is already bound by a live record to a DIFFERENT canonical locator that is PRESENT and bears that same rootId is STORAGE_ROOT_COLLISION. Neither root is selected, no projects/<ProjectId> beneath either is opened, and no authority record is created, read for resolution, or switched.
resolutionExits: (a) EXPLICIT ADOPT/MOVE, permitted only after the bound locator is proven ABSENT: one atomic locator rebind at unchanged rootId and unchanged authority generation, because a move changes the locator and not the identity.
(b) EXPLICIT FORK, which allocates a fresh rootId into the copy under create-new plus fsync before that copy may be admitted at all.
SN-P2.whyNotACreateTimeCheck: Copying an admitted root — backup restore, cp -r, disk image, container layer, cloud-sync duplicate — happens outside the tool, so no check performed at creation can observe it. Uniqueness therefore has to be a property the OPEN path evaluates. That is what lets this contract use the word unique at all, which the predecessor never did.
SN-P2.inexpressibility: The record set cannot record the ambiguity: writing the second, disagreeing binding IS the invariant violation. 'One rootId at two live roots' has no representation it could later be resolved from, so there is no ambiguous durable state for a recovery rule to arbitrate.
SN-P2.noNewDurableStructure: The registry this ranges over is the set of records at authorityRecordPath, which the predecessor already names 'the user-scoped authority registry' in inventory.userAuthority. No field is added to authorityRecordExactFields and no store is introduced.

SN-P3.title: An admitted root is one device across the rename operand set its own layout derives.
SN-P3.statement: A storage root is admitted only if the root itself, projects/, control/, quarantine/ and every directory beneath projects/ and quarantine/ report one device identity, and no path within that scope is a mount point. The property is captured from the retained root handle at admission and re-established at every re-admission. A root that fails it is refused with STORAGE_ROOT_NOT_ONE_DEVICE before any user-derived durable write, rather than being discovered partway through a durable state machine.
SN-P3.whyControlIsInScope: The purge journal at layout.purgeJournal and the namespace it describes are read TOGETHER by purge.recoveryRule. A journal that could outlive its namespace across a device boundary would make the recovery table read two independently failing devices, which is a worse defect than the rename failure itself.
SN-P3.admissionCost: The predicate ranges over DIRECTORIES. That set is bounded by the layout and by the number of projects and in-flight operations; it does not range over CAS objects, so admission does not become linear in stored evidence.
SN-P3.whyNotAnEighthCapabilityPredicate: pathSafety.unsupported is a list of capability predicates, and 'the root is one filesystem' is a scope property rather than a filesystem capability, so it could not be expressed there. The repair retypes the DOMAIN of those predicates to the operands of the operation instead of adding a member, which is why the list is unchanged.

SN-P4.title: Authority-record creation is compare-and-swap at generation 0 -> 1, not a second mechanism.
SN-P4.statement: The generation-1 record is written create-new plus fsync under the authority lease at first durable write for that ProjectId, after the chosen root has been admitted. create-new IS the compare-and-swap with an empty baseline: a losing create-new is a losing compare-and-swap with the same refusal, so the record the predecessor said resolution 'trusts only' now has a specified birth that introduces no mechanism the predecessor had not already specified for the switch.
SN-P4.ordering: Admit the root (SN-P2, SN-P3) -> create the generation-1 record naming its rootId -> create projects/<ProjectId>. The record precedes the namespace, so a namespace can never exist for a ProjectId whose record does not name the root it sits under, which is exactly the condition SN-P5 refuses.
SN-P4.crashRecovery: A crash between record creation and namespace creation leaves a generation-1 record and no namespace. That is the defined pre-first-write state and is completed idempotently under the lease at the root the record already names — never by choosing a different root. A crash before record creation leaves neither, and the operation restarts from selection.

SN-P5.title: A namespace is never created fresh under a root the record does not name, and never silently adopted.
SN-P5.statement: projects/<ProjectId> may be brought into existence only by (a) allocation in the same lease-held operation that writes that ProjectId's generation-1 authority record for that root, or (b) the migration install rename onto a target the journal already reserved. Finding a canonical projects/<ProjectId> under an admitted root that no live authority record binds is STORAGE_NAMESPACE_ORPHANED and requires an explicit adopt.
SN-P5.whatItCloses: The predecessor's own stated consequence — 'projects/<ProjectId> is then created fresh there and the project is split across two physical namespaces with no specified corruption signal'. This is that signal. It also covers the case where the user-state authority record is lost while the durable evidence survives, which SN-P1 alone would silently treat as a project that has no storage.
SN-P5.inventoryAlreadyReportsIt: inventory.root already separates a corrupt-orphan class. The predecessor could REPORT this state and had no rule that made resolution REFUSE on it; SN-P5 connects the two and adds no reporting vocabulary.

renameAtomicity.derivation: The set of atomic-rename operand pairs is DERIVED from layout rather than enumerated beside it. Every whole-namespace rename this contract defines has one endpoint under projects/ and the other under quarantine/ of the same admitted root, which is what makes a single device predicate over those two subtrees sufficient for all of them.
renameAtomicity.statedOnce: The precondition is stated once, at pathSafety.resolution, which is the rule both state machines already defer to for 'atomically rename only within one admitted root'. No branch is added to any operationOrdering step, no state is added, and no state machine is edited.
renameAtomicity.reachOfTheAdmissionScan: The admission scan observes DIRECTORIES. A file-level bind mount, and any mount created after admission, are outside what it can see. Neither is absorbed silently — see runtimeResidual — and this bound is stated rather than a totality claimed.
renameAtomicity.runtimeResidual: If the device property is violated after admission, every rename in the derived operand set refuses and PERSISTS NO STATE TRANSITION. The project is then fail-closed under the predecessor's existing rule that storage admission for that ProjectId refuses while any non-COMPLETE journal exists, and the next root admission refuses the root by SN-P3 and names the device split, so an operator receives a root-level diagnosis instead of a repeating opaque failure. No bytes are lost and no deletion is partially committed.

recoveryTableClosure.statement: Both crash-recovery tables are total over (reachable durable nonterminal state x observable path-presence tuple). Their DOMAIN IS DURABLE STATE, not operational outcome.
recoveryTableClosure.admissibilityTestForAFurtherRow: A further row becomes admissible if and only if states or reachableDurableNonterminalStates gains a member — that is, only if some operation can PERSIST a durable state the closed set does not contain. An operation that refuses without persisting a transition contributes no point to the domain, because the durable state after it is identical to the state before it.
recoveryTableClosure.appliedToTheCrossDeviceRefusal: The refused rename persists nothing, so it adds no point and requires no row. Purge stays at exactly 6 rows and migration at exactly 10. This is precisely why SN-P3 is an ADMISSION property and not a failure branch: a branch would have had to persist something to be reachable from the table, and persisting a new state is exactly what would have forced a seventh row.
recoveryTableClosure.measuredRatherThanArgued: Reproduced on a real nested mount on the authoring host: with the moving marker already written and fsynced inside the canonical namespace, the purge commit rename returned EXDEV (errno 18), leaving journal PREPARED, canonical present and quarantine absent. That tuple is row 1 of the closed purge table, 'PREPARED|canonical-present|quarantine-absent' -> resume-atomic-quarantine. The observation is a fact about rename(2) on that host, not about any built storage engine.
recoveryTableClosure.whatWouldFalsifyThis: Exhibit a step in either operationOrdering that can leave a journal in a state outside states, or leave a path-presence tuple no existing row covers while the journal reads a member of reachableDurableNonterminalStates. Either exhibit forces a row and falsifies this closure claim.

outcomes.rule: Internal diagnostic detail only. This artifact mints NO D9 class, error code or exit code and extends no D9 vocabulary. Projection reuses the rule resolved-inputs.v2.json#projectIdContract.identityOutcomeD9Mapping already binds — select provenance first, then project onto an existing context — and uses only its three existing closed provenance values.

STORAGE_ROOT_CALLER_SUPPLIED.meaning: A root reached a storage-resolution path. Under SN-P1 there is no such argument position, so this outcome exists to be unreachable in a conforming host and detectable in a non-conforming one.

STORAGE_ROOT_UNVERIFIED.meaning: An opened root's storage-root.v1.json is absent, malformed, not exactly {schemaVersion, rootId}, or fails the rootId pattern or the exact-type admission gate of IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §6 law 18.
STORAGE_ROOT_UNVERIFIED.provenance: callerOrConfig at selection; persistedMarkerOrRegistry at re-admission of a previously bound root

STORAGE_ROOT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH.meaning: The root reached through the advisory locator bears a rootId that is not byte-equal to the record's activeRootId. No namespace is opened and no locator is rebound.

STORAGE_ROOT_COLLISION.meaning: One rootId is present at two live canonical locators. Neither is selected.

STORAGE_ROOT_LOCATOR_STALE.meaning: The bound locator is absent. This is the precondition for the one permitted atomic rebind, not a failure of identity; it requires an explicit adopt and never an implicit one.

STORAGE_ROOT_NOT_ONE_DEVICE.meaning: The layout-derived rename operand scope of the root does not resolve to one device identity, or contains a mount point.

STORAGE_NAMESPACE_ORPHANED.meaning: A canonical projects/<ProjectId> exists under an admitted root that no live authority record binds. Reported by inventory in its existing corrupt-orphan class; refused by resolution.

outcomes.whyTheseAreNamed: An outcome with no name is how the predecessor arrived at a durable field with no consumer. Each value above is produced by exactly one property and consumed by the provenance rule the identity owner already binds; none is decorative.

fixtures.enforcementDisclosure: These vectors are DECLARED and are NOT enforced by check-threat-claims.py, whose T13 fixture assertion is a closed set equality over storageNamespace.fixtures and would reject an addition there. They were deliberately placed in this sibling so that applying this derivation does not require shipping a checker in the same act. Until a successor checker enforces them they are specification text and not a regression instrument, and physicalIsolationConformance.paperSealRule applies to them exactly as it applies to everything else here.

vectors.scenario: a caller passes an admitted, well-formed, device-clean root to a storage-resolution path
activeRootCanonicalPath resolves to a well-formed admitted root whose rootId differs from activeRootId
an admitted root is copied whole; original and copy are both present and their markers are byte-identical; the copy is offered for admission
the same root is renamed rather than copied, so the bound locator is absent and exactly one root bears that rootId
vectors.expected: STORAGE_ROOT_LOCATOR_STALE, then one atomic locator rebind at unchanged rootId and unchanged generation under explicit adopt

vectors.scenario: a filesystem is mounted at projects/<ProjectId> beneath an otherwise valid root
vectors.expected: STORAGE_ROOT_NOT_ONE_DEVICE at admission, before any user-derived durable write

vectors.scenario: projects/<ProjectId> is present under an admitted root and no live authority record names that ProjectId at that root

observabilityBoundary.rule: Every property in this section is a property of the SPECIFICATION. Whether a built host honours SN-P1..SN-P5 is a runtime question, is release-gated under G14, and no instrument in this corpus can observe it. This artifact declares no demonstration evidence and asserts no coverage over a built storage engine.
whatIsObservableHere: that activeRootId has a specified consumer, and which one
that the authority-record set can express at most one live locator per rootId
that the rename operand set is derived from layout and is finite
that the closure test deciding whether a further recovery row is admissible is stated, together with what would falsify it
observabilityBoundary.whatIsNotObservableHere: The five PI-* observations. This artifact offers no verdict on them and changes nothing about them: state stays SPECIFIED, evidenceGrade stays IMPLEMENTABLE_UNEXECUTED, gateIds stays ['G14'], demonstrationEvidenceIds stays empty. IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md §7 records claiming a region no instrument can observe as this corpus's dominant failure mode; declining is the correct result and not a coverage gap.
